summary: Full-extraction pass over 13 stored Hong Kong LegCo documents (CIES 2004-2018 replies and annexes, a 2010 Security Panel paper, New CIES replies of 2024-2025). Most numbers were already in the dataset; this pass adds 21 observations (real-estate split and shares, a property-district sample, averages, expectations, rounded New CIES pipeline counts, dependants in entry applications, property-market shares), 10 term rows and one event. Two documents stay partial.

observations.quote: Of the $14.35 billions in real estate investment under the CIES
observations.notes: Total real-estate investment under the CIES; the reply does not give the cut-off date for this figure (para (a) counts approvals to end of March 2010, and the annex's real-estate total to March 2010 is 14,352 million). Printed with a bare '$'; recorded as HKD following existing Hong Kong rows (Hong Kong Government replies use $ for Hong Kong dollars; the annex to the same reply heads its table 'Millions Hong Kong Dollars'). Pending decision on bare '$' in Hong Kong documents.

observations.quote: residential and non-residential properties amounted to $13.35 billion (93%) and $1 billion (7%) respectively
observations.notes: Share of REAL-ESTATE investment ($14.35 billion), not of all CIES investment. Cut-off date not given (see the 14.35 row).

observations.quote: residential and non-residential properties amounted to $13.35 billion (93%) and $1 billion (7%) respectively
observations.notes: Share of REAL-ESTATE investment ($14.35 billion), not of all CIES investment. Cut-off date not given (see the 14.35 row).

observations.quote: The great majority of applicants who invested in residential properties only invested in a single property, with an average value of around $10 million.
observations.notes: Average value of the single residential property bought by the great majority of applicants investing in residential property; rounded ('around'). Period not given (reply dated 5 May 2010); dataset convention 'to <date>' with basis unspecified. Printed with a bare '$'; recorded as HKD following existing Hong Kong rows (Hong Kong Government replies use $ for Hong Kong dollars; the annex to the same reply heads its table 'Millions Hong Kong Dollars'). Pending decision on bare '$' in Hong Kong documents.

observations.quote: Kowloon West 29%
observations.notes: Location of the properties invested in, 'Based on an analysis of 200 recent applications' (a sample, not all applicants); table total printed as 100%. Base is the properties in those applications as printed. Period not given (reply dated 5 May 2010); dataset convention 'to <date>' with basis unspecified.

observations.quote: Hong Kong Island 25%
observations.notes: Location of the properties invested in, 'Based on an analysis of 200 recent applications' (a sample, not all applicants); table total printed as 100%. Base is the properties in those applications as printed. Period not given (reply dated 5 May 2010); dataset convention 'to <date>' with basis unspecified.

observations.notes: Location of the properties invested in, 'Based on an analysis of 200 recent applications' (a sample, not all applicants); table total printed as 100%. Base is the properties in those applications as printed. Period not given (reply dated 5 May 2010); dataset convention 'to <date>' with basis unspecified.

observations.quote: Kowloon East 14%
observations.notes: Location of the properties invested in, 'Based on an analysis of 200 recent applications' (a sample, not all applicants); table total printed as 100%. Base is the properties in those applications as printed. Period not given (reply dated 5 May 2010); dataset convention 'to <date>' with basis unspecified.

observations.notes: Location of the properties invested in, 'Based on an analysis of 200 recent applications' (a sample, not all applicants); table total printed as 100%. Base is the properties in those applications as printed. Period not given (reply dated 5 May 2010); dataset convention 'to <date>' with basis unspecified.

observations.quote: the Capital Investment Entrant Scheme ("CIES") had brought around $50 billion of investments to Hong Kong since its implementation in October 2003
observations.notes: The legislator's question relaying the Secretary for Security's statement at the Council meeting of 21 April 2010; rounded ('around'). End date = date of the statement. Printed with a bare '$'; recorded as HKD following existing Hong Kong rows (Hong Kong Government replies use $ for Hong Kong dollars; the annex to the same reply heads its table 'Millions Hong Kong Dollars'). Pending decision on bare '$' in Hong Kong documents.

observations.quote: The annual application figure jumped from 465 in 2004 to 2 997 this year (up to November 22)
This amount is less than 1% of the total trading volume in the property market in the same period (around HK$2.2 trillion [Note: 1])
observations.notes: 'Less than 1%' recorded as 0 to 1. Numerator: HK$10.4 billion CIES property investment since October 2003; denominator (Note 1): total consideration of sale and purchase agreements of building units from 2004 to the first half of 2009. Status 'estimate' as for the LCQ7 2011 row of the same indicator.

observations.quote: Their investments amount to about HK$796 million in total, representing an average of HK$7.17 million per entrant.
observations.notes: Average investment per entrant among the 111 entrants granted formal approval by 29 May 2004.

observations.quote: It is expected that the 82 applicants granted "approval-in-principle" will invest not less than HK$500 million in the next few months.
observations.notes: Expected investment by the 82 applicants holding approval-in-principle; lower bound ('not less than'). Date = date of the reply.

observations.quote: In other words, the Scheme has so far been able to attract investments of over HK$1.3 billion to Hong Kong.
observations.notes: Lower bound ('over'). Combines about HK$800 million already invested by the 111 formally approved entrants and the HK$500 million expected from the 82 holding approval-in-principle, so part of it is an expectation: status projection. The '(about) HK$800 million' in the same paragraph is a rounding of the HK$796 million already recorded and is not added again.

observations.quote: Since the launch of the New CIES on March 1 up to end-May, InvestHK received over 3 000 enquiries (mainly from the potential applicants and service providers)
observations.notes: Printed as 'over 3 000' (lower bound). Includes enquiries from service providers.

observations.quote: and received over 250 applications
observations.notes: Printed as 'over 250' (lower bound); the annex gives the exact count, 251.

observations.quote: The Net Asset Assessment for over 100 applications was approved.
observations.notes: Printed as 'over 100' (lower bound); the annex gives 103.

observations.quote: The ImmD granted "approval-in-principle" for over 40 applications
observations.notes: Printed as 'over 40' (lower bound); the annex gives 43.

observations.location: Annex p. 1, table 'Assessment of applications under the New CIES (as of end-May 2024)', column 'Entry applications received by ImmD', Total row
observations.quote: (Number of dependants: 190)
observations.notes: Dependants covered by the 90 entry applications received by ImmD (main applicants' entry applications counted separately as 90).

observations.quote: Investment on real estate since the launch of the scheme is around HK$11.7 billion, representing less than 1% of the volume of the total transaction of local property market from 2004 to the first half of 2009 (around HK$2,474.1 billion).
observations.notes: 'Less than 1%' recorded as 0 to 1. Numerator: CIES real-estate investment since launch (October 2003); denominator: total local property transactions 2004 to first half of 2009. The 'around HK$11.7 billion' is a rounding of the Annex II real-estate figure (11,671.5 million) already recorded and is not added again.

program_terms.quote: We are of the view that the current investment threshold of HK$6.5 million under our Scheme is comparable to those of other advanced economies.
program_terms.notes: Threshold in force at the date of the reply (9 June 2004); launch date 27 Oct 2003 from para (a). Investment in real estate and/or specified financial assets (equities, debt securities, certificates of deposit, subordinated debt, eligible unit trusts or mutual funds), switchable at any time (para (c)). End date not in this document.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.quote: Applicants are required to have net assets of not less than HK$6.5 million throughout the two years preceding their applications.
program_terms.notes: Rule as described in the paper of December 2009 (launch 'October 2003'). End date not in this document.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (with spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18)
program_terms.quote: not less than HK$6.5 million in permissible investment asset classes, including real estate3 and financial assets4
program_terms.notes: Para 6: applicants invest within six months before applying or within six months after approval-in-principle. Real estate (commercial, industrial or residential, footnote 3) and financial assets (equities, debt securities, certificates of deposit, subordinated debts, eligible collective investment schemes, footnote 4). End date not in this document. The 3 and 4 in the quote are footnote markers.

program_terms.quote: Under the New CIES, applicants must invest a minimum of HK$30 million in the permissible investment assets
including investing a minimum of HK$27 million in the permissible financial assets and/or real estate (subject to a cap of HK$10 million)
program_terms.notes: Real estate counts for at most HK$10 million (a cap, not a minimum; not a separate row).

program_terms.quote: and placing HK$3 million into a new Capital Investment Entrant Scheme Investment Portfolio (CIES Investment Portfolio)
with effect from October 16, 2024, applicants under the New CIES are allowed to invest in residential properties, provided that the transaction price of a single property is HK$50 million or above
program_terms.notes: All real estate together still counts for at most HK$10 million toward the threshold.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.quote: not less than HK$30 million net throughout six months (two years before the enhancement) preceding the application
program_terms.notes: Two-year holding period before the enhancement effective 1 March 2025.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets (jointly owned family assets count for the applicant's share), held throughout the six months before applying
program_terms.quote: An applicant under the New CIES is only required to demonstrate that he/she has net assets or net equity to which he/she is absolutely beneficially entitled with a market value of not less than HK$30 million net throughout six months
Under the Scheme, applicants must invest a minimum of HK$30 million in the permissible investment assets.

events.title: Insurance products reported as added to permissible assets
events.description: The Secretary for Security tells LegCo on 11 November 2009 that the Government 'has recently included' insurance products meeting the relevant requirements as permissible CIES investment assets. The date of the change is not given; the month is the date of the statement. Another source dates the inclusion of investment-linked assurance scheme products to 6 July 2010 (event e-29ea5f8568); the two may describe different steps or the same change.
events.quote: The Government has recently included insurance products satisfying the relevant requirements as permissible investment assets.

new_indicators.name: Average investment per investor (or per property)
new_indicators.definition: Average qualifying investment per investor, or average value of the asset bought (e.g. per property), under a residence- or citizenship-by-investment programme in a period, as printed by the source. Never calculated by us. Notes say what the average is taken over.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-hkg3 for Hong Kong LegCo replies: HK$7.17 million per CIES entrant (LCQ15, 9 June 2004) and an average residential property value of around $10 million (LCQ12, 5 May 2010).

gaps: Annex to LCQ13 (2 Dec 2009) comparing overseas investor schemes is not stored.

ledger.contains: LegCo written reply (5 May 2010) on the CIES: cumulative approvals to March 2010 (6,689); real-estate investment of $14.35 billion split residential $13.35 billion (93%) / non-residential $1 billion (7%); average single residential property around $10 million; district shares of properties from a sample of 200 recent applications; 10 of 100 recently approved extension cases had changed property; the questioner's 'around $50 billion' total; review timing. Yearly tables are in the separate annex (hkg-legco-lcq12-cies-2010-annex). Part (h) gives General Employment Policy entrepreneur figures (775 entrepreneurs 2007-2009; 100-case sample by sector, jobs and investment): a different scheme, out of scope. Bare '$' recorded as HKD following existing Hong Kong rows (pending decision).
ledger.to_do: Not recorded: 'among the 100 extension cases approved recently, only 10 applicants have changed their properties' (a count from a sample of 100 renewals; no indicator fits, and turning it into a percentage would be a calculation).

ledger.contains: Annex to LCQ12 (5 May 2010): approved applicants by type (Chinese nationals with overseas permanent residence, foreign nationals, others) for 2003-2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, Jan-Mar 2010 and total; investment value (HK$ million) by real estate and specified financial assets (equities, debt securities, collective investment schemes, others) for the same periods. All rows and columns add to the printed totals (6,689; 47,262). Everything was already in the dataset; no new rows.

LegCo written reply (2 Dec 2009): about HK$36.6 billion investment since Oct 2003 incl. HK$10.4 billion in property; property investment under 1% of property trading volume (about HK$2.2 trillion, 2004 to H1 2009); 5,604 principal applicants formally approved to 22 Nov 2009; applications 465 in 2004 and 2,997 in 2009 to 22 Nov; 53 refusals. Not recorded: the 'just 0.2% of Hong Kong households' figure (an illustrative ratio built on the stated assumption that each approved applicant is one household, not a programme statistic) and the HK$2.2 trillion market total (context, not the programme). The annex comparing overseas investor schemes is not stored. New rows: 2004 applications (465) and the under-1% property share.

LegCo written reply (9 June 2004): applications to 29 May 2004 (339) by applicant category, formal approvals (111) by investment type, approvals-in-principle (82), one rejection, investment of about HK$796 million (financial assets 509, real estate 287), average HK$7.17 million per entrant, expected HK$500 million from AIP holders and 'over HK$1.3 billion' combined; HK$6.5 million threshold; comparisons with other countries' thresholds (HK$2 million to over HK$10 million; Singapore S$1.5 million), which concern other programmes and are not recorded. 'About HK$800 million' in para (b) is a rounding of the 796 already recorded. New: average investment (new indicator rbi_investment_average), expected investment, combined HK$1.3 billion (projection) and a threshold term row.
Annex A to LCQ15 (9 June 2004): nationalities of the 137 foreign-national applicants (30 countries). Adds up to 137. All already in the dataset; no new rows.
Annex B to LCQ15 (9 June 2004): country of permanent residence of the 158 Chinese-national applicants (18 countries). Adds up to 158. All already in the dataset; no new rows.

LegCo written reply (11 Nov 2009): 5,182 applicants and 9,945 dependants approved to end-Sep 2009, by applicant category; investment of HK$36,665.1 million by six asset classes (adds up); 53 refusals; yearly applications 2004 to Jan-Sep 2009; insurance products recently added as permissible assets; seven-year residence rule for permanent residence. Numbers were all already in the dataset; adds one event (insurance products added, date not given). The $6.5 million threshold appears only in the question and is recorded from other sources.

LegCo written reply (12 June 2024) on the New CIES: enquiries (over 3,000), applications (over 250), net-asset assessments approved (over 100) and approvals-in-principle (over 40) to end-May 2024; detail in the annex; InvestHK briefings for around 2,000 industry participants and promotion plans (outreach, not programme statistics; not recorded). New: the four rounded counts (lower bounds).

Annex to LCQ15 (12 June 2024): New CIES assessment pipeline to end-May 2024 by applicant category (NAA received/approved, entry applications, AIP, investment requirement approved, formal approval), dependants in entry applications (190), age of applicants (Table 1, adds to 251), country of the 245 foreign/overseas-PR applicants for NAA and entry applications (Table 2, adds to 245 and 88). Note 1 (permission to stay up to 24 months) is a rule, not an amount. All numbers were already in the dataset except the 190 dependants (added).

LegCo written reply (16 April 2025): New CIES applications in March 2025 (174), NAA approved (99), entry applications (65) by country (adds to 65), over HK$5.2 billion expected if all approved, 1,092 applications since March 2024, HK$30 million minimum, AIP assessment in around three weeks; AML duties of intermediaries; March 2025 enhancements; unrelated parts on cross-boundary remittance and talent schemes (out of scope). Statements that no application had been rejected or granted approval-in-principle are words, not counts. New: one term row (HK$30 million).
ledger.to_do: Not recorded: 'The ImmD will generally complete the assessment of "approval-in-principle" in around three weeks' (processing_time_months is in months; converting weeks would be a calculation). Also for review: the existing row o-17157f5c8a (applications_rejected = 0) was made from the words 'no application has been rejected so far'.

ledger.contains: LegCo written reply (12 Dec 2018) on the suspended CIES: yearly 2015 to Nov 2018 outstanding applications, refusals, approvals, persons acquiring right of abode, refused extensions of stay (columns (v) and (vi) not applicable per Note 3); rules on two-year extensions and no top-up requirement. All numbers already in the dataset; the $10 million threshold appears only in the question. No new rows.

LegCo written reply (26 March 2025) on the New CIES: to end-Feb 2025 918 applications, 868 NAA approved, 386 investment requirements approved, 756 approvals-in-principle, 341 formal approvals, over HK$27 billion expected; verified investment by asset class (adds to 10,548 million); no residential property investment yet (words); thresholds (HK$30m total, HK$27m assets, HK$10m real-estate cap, HK$3m portfolio, HK$50m residential from 16 Oct 2024) and the 1 March 2025 enhancements (six-month net-asset test, family holding vehicles). Numbers were already in the dataset; adds six term rows from this source.

LegCo Panel on Security paper (Dec 2009 / 5 Jan 2010) on the Quality Migrant Admission Scheme (QMAS, a talent scheme: applications, outcomes and applicant profiles in para 3-5 and Annex I; out of scope) and the CIES: rules (HK$6.5m net assets for two years; HK$6.5m investment), 5,676 principal applicants and 10,871 dependants approved to Nov 2009 by category (top three foreign nationalities named without counts), yearly applications 2004 to Jan-Nov 2009, investment of HK$40,124.8 million by six asset classes (Annex II, adds up), property investment around HK$11.7 billion = under 1% of property transactions 2004 to H1 2009. New: the under-1% share and two term rows.
